title: Day 61 · Week 8, Day 5 — Protocol: the pregnancy file — five sections, every first-visit number with its threshold, the women who carried their own notes, and the law that makes the results hers the moment they exist
summary: The fifth Protocol episode, and the folder the loose pages since Day 35 go into. Your baby is at Carnegie stage 19 (16–18 mm), trunk lengthening, head lifting, elbows bent with the hands meeting — and about to be measured crown to rump for the first time. Why a record she holds: Cochrane 2015 (Brown et al.; 4 trials, 1,176 women): women carrying their own notes felt in control (RR 1.56, 1.18–2.06), wanted to carry them again (RR 1.79), lost them no more often — and the honest odd signal of more caesareans (RR 1.51) and operative deliveries (RR 1.83) in two single trials; NICE NG201 on updating the record at every visit. Section one, dates: LMP, cycle, the Day 28 due date, CRL and the ACOG CO 700 redating rule; the schedule — US monthly/fortnightly/weekly, 12–14 visits codified in 1930 (Peahl & Howell 2021), NICE's 10 appointments for a first pregnancy and 7 thereafter with two scans, WHO's 8 contacts. Section two, the numbers with thresholds: blood pressure as the baseline (ALSPAC, 13,016 women: later-hypertensive women already higher at 8 weeks — Macdonald-Wallis 2012), 140/90 on two readings 4 h apart, 160/110 same-day (ACOG, NICE), pre-eclampsia ~4% US (USPSTF 2017, grade B for BP at every visit) and up to 8% globally, aspirin 81 mg from 12–28 weeks for risk factors, and the BUMP trials (Tucker, Chappell 2022: 2,441 and 850 women; self-monitoring detected hypertension no earlier and controlled it no better); IOM 2009 weight bands by BMI; the Day 50 blood-count lines (Hb 11, ferritin 30, MCV, platelets); blood group, Rh and the 28-week antibody repeat; the four infection screens with their reasons — hepatitis B (≈17,800 US infants a year born to carriers, 0.5% of births; ~90% of perinatally infected infants chronic, a quarter of those dying of liver disease — CDC), HIV (15–45% transmission untreated — WHO), syphilis (3,882 congenital cases and 279 stillbirths/infant deaths in 2023; ~40% of babies of untreated mothers stillborn or dying — CDC), rubella (Miller 1982: defects in every infected infant before week 11, 35% at 13–16 weeks, none after 16); urine culture — 2–10% prevalence, USPSTF 2019 grade B, Cochrane 2019 (15 trials: pyelonephritis RR 0.24, low birth weight RR 0.64, low certainty) against Kazemier 2015 (4,283 women: untreated bacteriuria pyelonephritis 2.4% vs 0.6%, no preterm excess). What isn't routine (TSH, vitamin D). Section three, the pages already made. Section four, how data arrives: Cures Act immediate release since 5 April 2021, HIPAA's 30 days, and Steitz 2023 (8,139 patients: 95.7% want immediate results, 7.5% more worried, over half then searched the internet). Section five, your page.
action: Twenty minutes tonight: building, not reading. One: a folder with five dividers, or a shared note on both phones with five headings — Dates, Numbers, Questions, Medicines, Us. Two: fill Dates from what you have: last period, cycle length, the Day 28 due date, the Day 40 scan date, and the appointment schedule you're on (two scans, the 24–28-week glucose test and the 27–36-week vaccine window pencilled in). Three: on Numbers, write the left-hand column and thresholds before any results exist — blood pressure (140/90; 160/110), weight and BMI with her IOM band, haemoglobin (11), ferritin (30), blood group and Rh with your type beside it, hepatitis B, HIV, syphilis, rubella immunity, chlamydia, urine culture, crown-rump length with the dating rule — and leave the right-hand column blank. Four: move the Day 40 sheet, the Day 42 card, the Day 54 medication list and the Day 60 insurance page into their dividers, and write the Day 28 after-hours number on the cover. Five: at this week's visit, ask how results are released, whether there is a portal and whether she wants you on it, and ask for a printed copy of the booking bloods. Then photograph every page.
